pr_body:
Fixes #11024.

This PR adds `require_always` option to `Style/EndlessMethod` that all endless method definitions are required.

```ruby
# EnforcedStyle: require_always

# bad
def my_method
  x
end

# bad
def my_method
  x.foo
   .bar
   .baz
end

# good
def my_method = x

# good
def my_method = x.foo
                 .bar
                 .baz
```

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].

* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [x] Added tests.
* [x] Ran `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and runs RuboCop on its own code.
* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

pr_comments: We'll have to think about the naming (or at least improve the high-level description for the new style), though, as now I find it to be somewhat confusing.

I've updated to `EnforcedStyle: require_endless_method`.

The `require_endless_method` style enforces endless method definitions for a single statement (not a single line) containing a method chain with a line break.

```ruby
# EnforcedStyle: require_endless_method

# bad
def my_method
  x
end

# bad
def my_method
  x.foo
   .bar
   .baz
end

# good
def my_method = x

# bad
def my_method = x.foo
                 .bar
                 .baz
```

Possibly a bit different than what #11024 wants, but it's simpler in name and behavior and always enforces `EnforcedStyle: require_endless_method`. cc @jonas054 

I also thought of `EnforcedStyle: single_line_endless_method` which allows the following case.

```ruby
# EnforcedStyle: single_line_endless_method

# bad
def my_method
  x
end

# bad
def my_method = x.foo
                 .bar
                 .baz

# good
def my_method = x

# good
def my_method
  x.foo
   .bar
   .baz
end
```

But its name and behavior are a little more complicated than `EnforcedStyle: require_endless_method`.

So, I've updated this PR using `EnforcedStyle: require_endless_method`. How about?

> require_endless_method

Or perhaps `always_require`?  I'll have to think about the naming here a bit more and how this will tie with `always_for_single_line` or something like this.

> Or perhaps `always_require`?

This name represents the current implementation that this PR adds. OHTH, there is already an option called `allow_always`, I updated it to `require_always` instead.

```diff
       # * allow_single_line (default) - only single line endless method definitions are allowed.
       # * allow_always - all endless method definitions are allowed.
       # * disallow - all endless method definitions are disallowed.
+      # * require_always - all endless method definitions are required.
```

After thinking about this a bit more - without something like `require_single_line` I think that the cop will remain to be pretty weird. I think the use cases for `require_always` will be relatively limited in comparison.

issue_context.title: How to enforce endless methods?
issue_context.body:
Hi, I'm trying to get Rubocop to replace one-liners with endless methods in ruby 3.0.2.

I've tried different combinations of the `Style/EndlessMethod` and `Style/SingleLineMethods` cops, without any success.

--------

## Expected behavior

Suppose I have a file called `example.rb` with the following code:

```ruby
class Example
  def a_method
    "42"
  end
end
```

And the following `.rubocop.yml` file:

```yml
Style/EndlessMethod:
  Enabled: true
  EnforcedStyle: allow_single_line
```

I'd expect `rubocop -a example.rb` to report the method as endless-able, and correct it to:

```ruby
class Example
  def a_method = "42"
end
```

## Actual behavior

I only see other cops being ran, but there's no trace of the `Style/EndlessMethod` cop:

```
❯ rubocop -c .rubocop.yml -A example.rb --debug
configuration from /tmp/.rubocop.yml
Default configuration from /Users/andreaschiavini/.rbenv/versions/3.0.2/lib/ruby/gems/3.0.0/gems/rubocop-1.36.0/config/default.yml
Inspecting 1 file
Scanning /tmp/example.rb
C

Offenses:

example.rb:3:1: C: Style/Documentation: Missing top-level documentation comment for class Example.
class Example
^^^^^^^^^^^^^
example.rb:5:5: C: [Corrected] Style/StringLiterals: Prefer single-quoted strings when you don't need string interpolation or special symbols.
    "42"
    ^^^^

1 file inspected, 2 offenses detected, 1 offense corrected
Finished in 0.13531199999852106 seconds
```


## Steps to reproduce the problem

This is extremely important! Providing us with a reliable way to reproduce
a problem will expedite its solution.

- create the ruby file above
- create the provided `.rubocop.yml` enabling the endless method cop
- run it

## RuboCop version

```
1.36.0 (using Parser 3.1.2.1, rubocop-ast 1.21.0, running on ruby 3.0.2) [arm64-darwin21]
```
comments:
There's no support currently for the functionality you want, but it should be possible to add. I also happen to think it makes sense to be able to enforce endless method definitions. Because I like them.

Let's say we want to support autocorrecting from
```ruby
class Example
  def a_method
    "42"
  end
end
```
via
```ruby
class Example
  def a_method; "42" end
end
```
to
```ruby
class Example
  def a_method = "42"
end
```
It would require changes in both `Style/SingleLineMethods` and `Style/EndlessMethod`. The easier of these two is `Style/EndlessMethod` becuase it has an `EnforcedStyle` configuration parameter and we can just add a supported style called `require_single_line` (meaning: require endless method definitions for methods that are defined on a single line). This would be backwards compatible. 

Fixing `Style/SingleLineMethods` is trickier bacause we don't have an `EnforcedStyle` there, only an `AllowIfMethodIsEmpty`. So how do we set up new config parameters to be able to enforce single line methods in a backwards compatible way? There's also a cop called `Layout/RedundantLineBreak`, which is disabled by default, but seems to be a candidate for enforcing single line methods too, although it doesn't do this currently.
👍 +1 would love to see this enhancement as well
I would love to see endless methods enforced by rubocop

review_comments: I see a possible problem if we report and autocorrect methods into endless methods that are too long for a single line. On the other hand, there's autocorrection in `Layout/LineLength` too, so some of these cases will be solved by the autocorrection loop.
I wasn't aware of this problem. I will take a look too.

hey @jonas054  + @koic . This has been sitting here for a while. This seems to be a relatively easy thing to fix. Haven't yet looked into how to find another cops definition but otherwise, it could be something like this:

```ruby
def handle_require_always_style(node)
  return if node.endless? || !node.body || node.body.begin_type? || node.body.kwbegin_type?

  line_length = node.body.source.length + definition.length
  return if line_length > config_store.line_length # or however this works

  add_offense(node, message: MSG_REQUIRE_ALWAYS) do |corrector|
    correct_to_endless_method(corrector, node)
  end
end

def definition(node) = "def #{node.method_name}#{arguments(node)} = "

def correct_to_endless_method(corrector, node)
  replacement = "#{definition(node)}#{node.body.source}"
  corrector.replace(node, replacement)
end
```
By the way, is there any difference between `EnforcedStyle: allow_always` and `Enabled: false`?

Ah, indeed it is!
It's possible that the option will be deprecated, but the incompatibility is annoying.
Good point. I'm guessing we can just issue some deprecation for `allow_always` and kill it in RuboCop 2.0 down the road. But it's not a big deal to keep it around.
